\section[das Rezept]{das Rezept — a prescription, a recipe}

\label{lesson:GE-C156-rezept}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the German for a traffic jam, then the German for an accident.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: das Rezept}
\textbf{das Rezept} — \textquotedblleft{}a prescription, a recipe\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{Rezept} $\leftarrow$ Latin \emph{receptum}, \textquotedblleft{}(what is) received\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB 2.1), from \emph{recipere}, \textquotedblleft{}to take\textquotedblright{} — borrowed. Doctors' prescriptions began \emph{recipe}, \textquotedblleft{}take!\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{Erkältung} is the noun of the verb \textquotedblleft{}to catch a chill\textquotedblright{}, Middle High German \emph{erkelten} (EtymDB 2.1): \emph{er-} + the word for \textquotedblleft{}cold\textquotedblright{}, Old High German \emph{kalt}, English \emph{cold}, + \emph{-ung}.
\end{cousinweb}
